subject: Behavioral Economics
title: The Endowment Effect on Income
description: A quick, practical guide to The Endowment Effect on Income.

hook.text: Getting a $10,000 raise feels good. Having $10,000 cut from your salary feels devastating.

buildup.text: Your current income becomes your reference point. Gains above it feel pleasant. Losses below it feel catastrophic.

discovery.text: This is why nominal pay cuts are nearly impossible even during recessions.

twist.text: Inflation is a 'hidden' pay cut that people accept because the nominal number doesn't drop. Real loss, zero outrage.

climax.text: Understanding income endowment helps negotiate: frame offers as gains above their current level, never as less.

punchline.text: People protect what they have more fiercely than they chase what they don't.

quiz.question: Why do companies avoid nominal pay cuts during recessions?
options: Workers treat current salary as a reference point; cuts feel like devastating losses
Companies have unlimited money during recessions
